daeva is to human as Daevite is to Roman.

"Daevite" is capitalized for the same reason that you capitalize "Roman" or "Gondolin". You don't capitalize "daeva" for the same reason you don't capitalize "human" or "elf" (or "elven").

"Daevite" is "of the civilization of the daeva" and "a Daevite" is "an anatomically modern human slave or daeva subject of the civilization of the daeva". A "daeva" is "a member of the non-Homo sapiens human species that ruled the Daevite civilization."

item.content:encoded:
I really love this SCP, I just have a few quibbles about the geography

Foundation archaeologists have discovered several sites containing ruins consistent with the supposed Daevite culture in various locations across Siberia, northern Iran, and Mongolia.

While Siberia and Mongolia make sense here, since Mongolia is directly south of much of central Siberia, northern Iran is quite some distance from either. You'd have to go through all of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan to reach northern Iran from Siberia.

Artifacts and traces of inter-cultural conflict and contact have been discovered as far west as the Carpathian Mountains and as far east as northern Pakistan and China.

Northern Pakistan is not east of central Siberia, it's mostly south and slightly west.

item.content:encoded:
If that website is trustworthy, then this is really disturbing.

I mean, think about it. Three species of primate that are nearly identical and have similar brain sizes living all at once is confusing enough, but the way they present the findings of DNA testing compared to the location of archaeological findings, something clearly isn't right.

I will note that that site declared that we share 99.8℅ of our DNA with chimps when other sites list it as 98.7℅ (which is actually a huge difference), so maybe it's not that accurate. Then again, other sites might be inaccurate.

Anyways, I honestly don't feel this has relevance to this article, but I'm now questioning the meaning of our existence and whether we truly know anything about the world we live in, so thanks for that.
